episodes.216905: Storms produced large hail across portions of central and north central South Dakota on the afternoon and evening of August 29th and into the early morning hours of August 30th. Hail to the size of golf-balls was observed in the town of Eureka and 4 miles northeast of Miller Dale Colony (Hand county).  Wind gusts with thunderstorms also produced some sporadic damage, with a power pole coming down at a residence 6 miles east of Lebanon (Potter county) and a number of calf shelters being shifted and tossed near Scatterwood Lake (Edmunds county).
episodes.216915: Thunderstorms produced sporadic high winds across mostly northeast South Dakota, with a 71 mph gust measured at the South Dakota Department of Transportation mesonet station 9 mile south southeast of Spink Colony.
episodes.217009: Pockets of heavy rain resulted in some localized flash flooding. In addition, a lightning strike resulted in a house fire.
episodes.217346: A complex of strong to locally severe thunderstorms, fueled by MLCAPE values in excess of 1000 J/KG and upper-level forcing from an approaching trough, materialized across much of southeastern AZ during the mid to late afternoon hours. Additional activity then developed across southern Gila County during the early evening hours. The thunderstorms resulted in rainfall rates in excess of 1 per hour with doppler radar rainfall totals estimated upwards of 1-2, enough to result in areas of flash flooding. Earlier in the day, an isolated strong thunderstorm developed near Stanfield with the downburst winds knocking down power poles near the Nissan Proving Grounds.
episodes.217562: An afternoon thunderstorm caused some damage to a structure due to a lightning strike.
episodes.217585: A heavier than average monsoon surge provided ample moisture for numerous showers and thunderstorms across the state.  Most notable of this was flash flooding in the Grand Canyon.  The results from these flash floods was the closure of Phantom Ranch, multiple inner canyon trails and the pipeline that provides water to the south Rim area breaking. Multiple people were rescued, and unfortunately 3 fatalities occurred from the flash flooding.
episodes.217884: Two days worth (27th and 28th) of southwesterly flow aloft was capped with an upper level low traversing the region on the 29th with a cold front. While none of the three days were particularly impressive from a setup perspective (Lacking one or more of forcing, thermodynamics, or kinematics), that did not stop the thunderstorms that formed from producing isolated severe reports.
episodes.217905: Scattered thunderstorms developed in a hot, moist airmass along outflow boundaries from the previous day���s convection. One of these storms moved through Bexar County between 7:45 PM and 9:00 PM on August 28th, causing widespread tree damage along a corridor from northeast Bexar County, through central San Antonio, and into southwest Bexar County. Scattered structural damage also occurred. Additionally, significant damage to power lines resulted in over 110,000 customers losing power at the peak of the storm. Storm surveys and radar data indicate that the damage is consistent with straight-line winds. Measured wind speeds reached 55 to 65 mph. Pockets of 70 to 80 mph winds were likely, estimated from radar and the resulting damage. The damage path was approximately 35 miles long, stretching from near Live Oak southwest into the Alamo Heights and Five Points areas, across the west side of San Antonio to Lackland AFB, and ending near Macdona in southwest Bexar County. The damage path was around two miles wide in northeast Bexar County, but widened to roughly five miles on the west and southwest sides of San Antonio, consistent with macroburst characteristics. Damage was estimated at $10 million.
episodes.217946: During the morning hours a series of thunderstorms tracked over Otter Tail County and heavy rainfall rates resulted in street flooding in Perham, MN.
episodes.217953: Though severe storms were primarily absent on the 29th, slow moving mainly scattered showers and thunderstorms developed during daytime heating south of a stationary frontal boundary. Very high available moisture resulted in several instances of very heavy rainfall across northeast FL.
episodes.218225: A weak frontal boundary slowing dropping southward into southern Georgia was the main driving force behind scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms, including isolated strong to severe thunderstorms during this period, along with the usual interactions with sea breeze/outflow interactions during strong diurnal heating. Many areas received 2+ inches or more of rainfall during this period thanks to very high available moisture and slow storm motion, though a report of isolated severe thunderstorm damage also occurred with this episode.
episodes.218263: A few severe thunderstorms impacted the southwestern portions of the state and brought hail and damaging winds.
episodes.218298: A cluster of strong to severe nocturnal thunderstorms produced between 50 and 60 mph winds. On the north edge of storms, a weak wake low developed in the stratiform area with spotty winds as strong or even a bit stronger from southern Lincoln and Lyon counties into Cottonwood County.
episodes.218460: Had thunderstorm winds gusts reach severe speeds and cause damage as well.
episodes.218480: With the subtropical ridge remaining in place, a stronger trough would impact the Pacific Northwest resulting in more widespread flash flooding across southern and central Utah, as well as widespread severe weather across the majority of Utah. This would go on to produce a prolific wind-driven hail event in Lynndyl, Utah.
episodes.218565: An upper trough coupled with a surface disturbance over the east-central Gulf favored an environment supportive of convection that produced strong marine wind gusts over Tampa and Sarasota Bay waters.
episodes.218592: An upper trough coupled with a surface disturbance over the east-central Gulf favored an environment supportive of convection that produced a fatal lightning strike near Saint Petersburg.

Wind driven hail with wind gusts potentially exceeding 100mph (per NWS storm survey) resulted in nearly every west facing vinyl wall needing replaced, as well as every roof needing replaced on roughly 52 homes. Crop damage was substantial, with nearly every cornfield damaged beyond repair. Additionally, numerous car windows were blown out by the hail with various other instances of damage reported.
